body:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: multiple pods in gpu-pool reporting OOM/Crashed and node ephemeral-storage pressure on node-45, node-46. Auto-escalation to #incidents (pager).
maria: seeing a flurry of `OOM` from modelcache pods, then several serving-runtime containers restarted. stack traces show CUDA OOM in logs. also /var/log on node-45 is 98% full.

maria: paste -- logs:
```
I0315 14:02:31.123 serving-runtime[pid=31415]: ERROR: cuda runtime error (2) : out of memory at ./src/cuda_utils.cu:452
I0315 14:02:31.124 serving-runtime[pid=31415]: FATAL: serving runtime aborting, signal 6
Mar 15 14:02:32 kubelet[1234]: Eviction manager: attempting to reclaim ephemeral-storage
Mar 15 14:02:32 kubelet[1234]: eviction signal observed: nodefs.available < eviction-threshold
```

kai (oncall): I'm paged, taking ownership. quick check: `kubectl get nodes -o=custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,EVP:.status.allocatable.storage` shows node-45 at 2% allocatable ephemeral.

kai (oncall): first mitigation: cordon node-45 and drain non-critical pods to avoid more evictions.
`kubectl cordon node-45`
`kubectl drain node-45 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`

ben: what about modelcache restart policy? we saw restarts cause synchronous reloads that spike disk writes. maybe disable startup prefetch.

maria: yes, modelcache config currently does full prefetch of indices on start. toggling to lazy load reduces disk churn. config snippet to patch:
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  modelcache.yaml: |
    prefetch_mode: lazy
    max_cache_bytes: 40GB
```
`kubectl apply -f modelcache-config-patch.yaml`

alex: ops-bot shows logrotate last ran 12d ago on node-45 (config rotates weekly by time rather than size). big logs from debug-level model loads filled /var/log. we should change to size-based rotate and compress.

sre-lead: agreed. immediate actions:
- reduce modelcache max cache to 40GB (patch applied)
- switch modelcache prefetch to lazy (patch applied)
- cordon/drain node-45 (kai)
- restart serving-runtime pods with `--enable-kv-cache=false` where safe to lower disk write amplification
- change logrotate on node pool to `maxsize 200M` + `rotate 7`

kai (oncall): applied cordon + drain. draining moved 6 pods off node-45, but 3 GPU-serving pods failed graceful shutdown and restarted on other GPUs, causing short-lived CUDA OOMs on node-46. I'm isolating remaining heavy pods to a new node-pool with larger ephemeral.

maria: traffic analysis: we saw ~12% of requests to some customers returned 503/timeout during 13:58-14:12 UTC. routing fallback activated for dedicated customers -> routed to regional fallback models. non-dedicated saw degraded latency and increased errors.

ben: opened incident ticket INC-2026-045 and added initial impact notes + Grafana links: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/serve/cluster-ephemeral?from=1670000000&to=1670002000 (link shortened)

ops-bot: :information_source: Auto-suggest: consider bumping kubelet eviction thresholds to give running jobs time to complete. Current flags: `--eviction-hard=imagefs.available<1%,nodefs.available<2%`. Suggest changing to `nodefs.available<1%,imagefs.available<0.5%` after we clean logs.

maria: I'm running the logcleanup script on node-45 to remove stale debug files: `ssh node-45 sudo /opt/reclaim/cleanup-logs --older-than 7d --prefix modelcache` disk usage dropping.

kai (oncall): after cleanup node-45 now 35% free. re-running `kubectl uncordon node-45` but leaving GPU-serving pods off until we finish config patches.
`kubectl uncordon node-45`

alex: proposing medium-term fixes:
- change modelcache to lazy prefetch by default
- add per-pod ephemeral storage requests/limits and CSI metrics for model cache directories
- convert heavy debug logs to `rotating_logger` with size cap so users don't accidentally fill nodefs
- add admission webhook to prevent new pods with huge `emptyDir` writes without quota

sre-lead: assign action items:
- alex -> PR for logrotate + node pool init scripts (ETA 3h)
- maria -> change modelcache helm chart values (done, will roll out canary)
- ben -> coordinate customer comms and provide SLA impact summary (ping customers affected)
- kai -> follow up on oncall shift handoff in 1h

kai (oncall): handoff to evening oncall in 1 hour. leaving note: "node-45 cleaned and uncordoned; modelcache patches rolled to 30% of cluster; monitoring alert thresholds temporarily relaxed to avoid noise; watching OOMs on node-46."

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident status: mitigation in progress, partial remediation applied. severity: P2 -> monitoring for 2 hours.

ben: customer impact draft: "Between 13:58-14:12 UTC a subset of inference requests (approx 12%) experienced errors or degraded latency due to node ephemeral-storage saturation triggering pod evictions and restarts. We mitigated by draining impacted nodes, reducing model cache prefetch, and cleaning logs. No data loss; customers on Dedicated had fallback routing applied. We will follow up with post-incident report and permanent changes to log rotation and cache defaults."

sre-lead: good. once evening oncall takes over, please check for any recurring restarts or CUDA errors. if repeats, open priority infra change to reserve ephemeral for modelcache dirs.

kai (oncall): handing off now to @eve (evening-oncall). leaving runbook note: `incident-evict-ephemeral.md` updated with steps taken and commands used.

maria: closing loop: confirm metrics back to baseline at 15:45 UTC, errors drop to <1% over 30m after canary rollout. will draft postmortem with timeline and follow-ups.

incident-bot: :lock: Incident moved to "monitoring"; responders: maria, kai, alex, ben.

(reacts: :thumbsup: from ben, :eyes: from sre-lead)
